trust_decision.summary: Whether a package-supplied numeric owner (uid/gid from /etc/passwd, /etc/group lines, APK tar headers, or installed-db M:/a: lines) fits a uint32 before it is narrowed and written back or applied; at the pinned commit every site parses into an int and narrows (or passes through) without a range check.

landing_point.why: Summary names /etc/passwd and /etc/group truncation; UserEntry.Parse does strconv.Atoi then uint32(uid) at :140, and the read-modify-write in pkg/build/accounts.go:101-145 persists it.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/apk/apk/installed.go:90-128 (AddInstalledPackage writes M:/a: owner lines) and pkg/apk/apk/installed.go:504-510 (parseInstalledPerms reads them back, including base-image idb via pkg/baseimg/base_image.go:106); also the archive decoder path pkg/apk/apk/install.go:232,437 in a different package from the passwd landing point

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about /etc/passwd and /etc/group text files; the APK installer and the installed-database M:/a: lines are a different file format in a different package (pkg/apk/apk), and memFS/tarfs WriteHeader does not even copy owners today (pkg/tarfs/fs.go:107-124), so a solver can argue those paths are not the reported truncation.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate owners up to MaxUint32 (4294967295, 2147483648 > MaxInt32, 65534 nobody, 0 root) must still parse, install and round-trip byte-identically; checkOwner on caller-built headers in AddInstalledPackage must not inherit the 32-bit refusal; parsing via ParseInt(...,32) or rejecting > MaxInt32 breaks them.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: pkg/passwd/passwd.go:157 (Write round-trip); fix.diff:117-127 (boundary matrix); fix.diff:250-255 (guard split)

O6_input_shapes: 32-bit int platform (linux/386, .goreleaser.yaml:21) where archive/tar narrows before apko sees the value

O7_producer.where: pkg/apk/apk/installed.go:118 and :128 (AddInstalledPackage emits M:/a: owner lines consumed by parseInstalledPerms pkg/apk/apk/installed.go:436,471); the narrowing producer for the 32-bit case is stdlib archive/tar, outside the repo

O8b_injection_room.sibling: NewAPKFS decodes package tar headers and stores header.Uid/Gid on each node with no range check; wiring it into an image emitter would be a realistic unvalidated decoder
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is an existing exported second APK reader (pkg/apk/fs/apkfs.go:75) that already copies owners; a maintainer adding a 'build from expanded APK FS' path would naturally reuse it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: uidGidFromInfo hands int owners from FileInfo.Sys() to the EROFS writer Chown (pkg/build/erofs.go:312, pkg/build/erofs_layers.go:393), the uint32 sink the fix comment names; a planted Sys() source carrying a raw decoded header would bypass install-time checks
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The function already trusts any *tar.Header in Sys(); a cache or layer-import path that returns the original header is a plausible addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: memFS.WriteHeader copying hdr.Uid/hdr.Gid onto the node (the 'natural completion of the mode/ownership work' per fix.diff:283-287)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix commit itself predicts this change; a planted version that copies owners before the check runs is a how-type ordering sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second passwd/group parser for Uname/Gname mapping using Atoi+int narrowing instead of passwd.ReadUserFile
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Name-mapping code is often reimplemented locally; currently it reuses the fixed parser.

O9_family: integer truncation / narrowing conversion of uid/gid (CWE-197) leading to privilege (root ownership) confusion
